newsitem.title: USA: Bill introduced to alter how Fed bank heads chosen.
newsitem.headline: Bill introduced to alter how Fed bank heads chosen.

text.p: House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach has introduced a bill to give the Federal Reserve Board in Washington the power to appoint the heads of regional Fed banks, a committee spokesman said on Monday.

Fed Bank presidents are currently chosen by the boards of their respective district banks. Those nine-person boards consist of six representatives elected by member banks from the district and three appointed by the Fed board here.
Under the bill introduced by Iowa Republican Leach, the seven-person Board here would appoint the president and the first vice president of the 12 district Fed banks.
The committee spokesman said the bill aims to do away with an apparent conflict of interest in having Fed bank presidents partly chosen by the commercial banks they oversee.
